Another practical example is: 「弟は勉強もしないで、遊んでばかりいる。」(My younger brother does not study at all and does nothing but play.) A quick test tip is to look at the preceding verb: since it is already in the て-form (飲んで), only 「ばかりいる」fits; eliminate 「ばかりに」(which follows the plain form) and 「ばかりでなく」(meaning “not only... but also”).

The grammar pattern 「〜ものの」 expresses a concessive contrast meaning “although..., but...”. It appropriately connects the preceding expectation of difficulty with the later reality that things were even harder than expected.

The complete sentence means: “Although I had expected it to be somewhat difficult, I never imagined it would actually be this challenging.” Example: 車を買ったものの、忙しくて運転する機会がほとんどない。 (Although I bought a car, I am so busy that I hardly ever have a chance to drive it.) default.q.test-8-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) 「〜あげく」describes a negative outcome after a long process of effort or inner conflict. It does not combine with a verb of cognition to mean concealing the truth.
